bib.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails". First author Zhou Yu (Salesforce AI; with Bin Bi, Shiva Kumar Pentyala, Shubham Mehrotra, Sougata Chaudhuri, Shilpa Bhagavath, Zeyuan Chen, Ran Xu, Phil Mui, James Zhu, Sitaram Asur). Preprint, arXiv:2609.09134v1 [cs.AI], 8 Sep 2026. No venue.
COVERAGE: 10 of 10 pages read; 39,124 of 39,124 chars. Text was clean. The last appendix (Case 2, Gemma Webarena) was cut off in my read after its first sentence, and I did not read the remainder. The figure caption was read in the text. I did not run the figures script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Fine-tuning the weaker model on full Gemini expert trajectories under the evolved harness h* lowers success on all 7 tasks.
 number: mean 78.0% -> 63.1% (-14.9); per-task range -4.2 (anomaly) to -29.9 (payroll)
 setup: qwen3-coder-30b-a3b (30B total, 3B active) student; gemini-3.1-pro-preview expert; LoRA-SFT; 7 enterprise tasks from Yang et al. 2026; test split; mean of 3 runs
 quote: "imitating the expert causes the weaker model to regress on all seven tasks (−4 to −30 points), a result reproduced across two model families (Qwen3-Coder and Gemma 4)" (p.1)
 Also: "this recipe lowers Qwen's mean test success from 78.0% to 63.1% (Table 1, rows 2 and 5)" (p.4)
 Largest drops: payroll -29.9, website -20.3, browser -16.0.
2. Rewriting only the failing turn in the student's own rollouts (SFT-corr.) matches or beats the evolved-harness baseline.
 number: 78.0% -> 79.7% (+1.7)
 setup: same Qwen student and h*; about 500 training rows; 3-run mean. Gains on 5 of 7 tasks: website +5.6, stock +2.2, refactor +2.2, anomaly +1.7, browser +1.2. Budget -0.6 and payroll -0.4 are within noise.
 quote: "it raises mean test success from 78.0% to 79.7% (+1.7), gaining on five of seven tasks" (p.7)
 The gain is small. Table 1 reports SEM (row 7 average ±0.67; row 2 ±0.97), so +1.7 is roughly 1-2 SEM, and the paper does not give a significance test.
3. The same imitation recipe helps under the unevolved baseline harness h0.
 number: 29.2% -> 35.5% (+6.3)
 quote: "raises Qwen's mean test success from 29.2% to 35.5% (Table 1, rows 1 and 6, +6.3 on average)" (p.4)
 The regression is therefore tied to the harness being evolved, not to imitation itself.
4. Harness evolution alone is the largest lever, and the expert uses the evolved harness even better.
 number: Qwen 29.2% -> 78.0% (+48.8); Gemini 84.4% -> 93.6% (+9.2)
 setup: GEPA-style search, with gemini-3.1-pro-preview as the reflection model and the harness evolved only with Qwen as executor. The budget was $20 per task per seed, with 3 seeds and a 600 s rollout limit (App. A).
5. Mechanism: imitation transfers knowledge but also the expert's planning style, which the weaker model cannot execute.
 number: planning failures rose from 1.1% to 14.6% of failures (+13.5) under imitation on h*, but only to 1.8% (+0.7) under correction. The implicit-knowledge share fell 46.2% -> 44.5% under imitation and 46.2% -> 43.2% under correction. Domain-computation recipe use rose 30.8% -> 76.1% after imitation. Overall failure rate under correction fell 28.9% -> 26.8%.
 setup: LLM-as-judge classification of failed rollouts into the six-category ontology of Yang et al. 2026 (App. C). These are shares of failures, not absolute rates.
 quote: "planning failures emerge as an essentially new failure mode, rising from 1.1% to 14.6% of failures (+13.5)" (p.6)
 Under h0, imitation also raised planning failures (0.9% -> 11.5%), but the knowledge gain dominated. The paper's explanation is that h0 was not fit to the model's planning, so there was no fit to lose.
 Case study (App. D, payroll): the imitated model gets the right answer but loops, re-issuing the same view 29 times and never finishing in 78 steps, so it scores 0.
6. A second model family shows the same regression, tested on one task only.
 number: Gemma-4-26b-a4b-it on Webarena: 46.7% -> 55.6% with h* (+8.9); after imitation 41.1% (14.5 below its h* baseline, 5.6 below its default-harness baseline). Gemini goes 71.1% -> 81.1%.
 quote: "fine-tuning the weak Gemma on the expert's trajectories again regresses it, to 41.1%" (p.5)

CO-EVOLUTION: Each round evolves a harness H*_t around model M_t, then updates the model under that harness to get M_{t+1}, and repeats (Fig. 1). The correction pipeline is driven by a "meta-level MLE agent" that localizes the failing turn. Only one round of correction is actually reported. The iterative loop is proposed, not demonstrated.
 Correction details (App. B): about 400 in-place expert-correction rows plus about 50 self-pass rows (rows the model passed itself). The expert is given the task, the trajectory up to that turn and the failed checkpoint. It writes one sentence of strategy plus the corrected tool call, with N=3 candidates and a quality judge picking the best.
 Training: LoRA rank 16 or 64 ("report the best scores"), 2 epochs, lr 1e-4, bf16, batch 8, sequence length 49,152, under an hour per run. The imitation arm used 3 LoRA seeds (0, 101, 202).
 Imitation data: expert trajectories scoring 1.0 plus the model's own passing rollouts.

BASELINES: the base harness h0 and evolved harness h* with unmodified Qwen (rows 1-2); Gemini expert on both harnesses (rows 3-4); SFT-imitation on h* and on h0 (rows 5-6); SFT-correction on h* (row 7). There is no RL baseline, no on-policy distillation baseline, no correction under h0, and no comparison with other correction methods such as Lauffer et al. 2025 or Ye et al. 2026.

LIMITS
- The authors concede correction "does not fully close the gap between the weaker and the expert model, likely due to a limit of the lightweight LoRA approach."
- One student family on 7 tasks (Qwen), plus Gemma on a single task. One expert (Gemini).
- LoRA only. Full fine-tuning is not tested, so the "planning-style drift" explanation is untested for it.
- Imitation data was filtered to score 1.0. Its size is not stated, so the imitation and correction arms are not size-matched (about 500 rows for correction). A data-quantity confound is therefore not ruled out.
- LoRA rank was chosen by best score, which is a selection effect.
- The causal story (planning-style drift) rests on an LLM-judge classification plus two case studies. The paper does not intervene on the planning style.
- The paper's own environment changes mean its absolute numbers are not comparable with Yang et al. 2026.
- Future work: RL combined with on-policy expert guidance, and harness evolution that is aware of later fine-tuning.

BUILDS ON: Yang et al. 2026 (task suite, harness adaptation, failure ontology); Agrawal et al. 2025 (GEPA); Lauffer et al. 2025 (on-policy expert corrections); Ye et al. 2026 (few teacher steps, on-policy augmentation); Hu et al. 2022 (LoRA); Wang et al. 2026 (Trajectory2Task, expert SFT); Xu et al. 2026 (upward harness transfer). Related joint-optimization work: SIA, Co-Harness, HarnessForge, HarnessX.

KEY QUOTES for the note
- "the weaker model adopts the expert's planning strategy without the competence to execute it and no longer fits the harness that was evolved around its native planning style" (abstract, p.1)
- "a meta-level MLE agent localizes the failing turn in each of the weaker model's own rollouts and has the expert rewrite only that turn, leaving the model's planning distribution intact" (p.2)
- "staying on-policy is what matters in the harness–model setting: the teaching signal is only useful when it respects the fit between the model and the harness it operates on" (p.8)

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.3), harness-model co-evolution loop. It is the only figure. Tables 1-3 carry the results.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The extraction is clean. Table 1 rows are flattened but legible. The reference list contains 2026 arXiv ids that I did not verify. I read the extracted text only, so the figure itself was not viewed. The "Gemma replication (Appendix C)" cross-reference in Appendix B is wrong, since Gemma appears in Sec 3.3.2 and App. D. The tail of App. D Case 2 was not read.
